subject: science
chapter_title: Cell: The Building Block of Life

primary.justification: The chapter's bulk — sections 2.2 through 2.3.1 and all organelle content-blocks — directly addresses C-3.1. It explains the semipermeability of the cell membrane (osmosis, diffusion, fluid-mosaic model), the cell wall's structural role, and the function of every named organelle (nucleus, ribosomes, ER, Golgi apparatus, lysosomes, mitochondria, plastids, vacuoles), making the cell the structural and functional unit of living organisms.

Sections 2.4, 2.4.1 (Mitosis, Meiosis), 2.5, and 2.5.1 form a cognitively distinct second strand on heredity mechanisms. The chapter introduces chromosomes, DNA, genes, and chromatin as carriers of hereditary information, and explains how mitosis preserves genetic identity across body cells while meiosis produces gametes with half the chromosome number, creating variation. This strand is carried in its own named sections and sections and is independent of the organelle content.

dissolution_test: This chapter builds the student's ability to explain how a cell's organelles (including the semipermeable membrane, nucleus, ER, Golgi, mitochondria, plastids, and vacuoles) make it the structural and functional unit of life AND how cell division — mitosis preserving chromosome number, meiosis halving it — transmits the DNA/chromosomal basis of heredity and enables variation, by comparing cell types through observation and tracing the flow from DNA to chromosome to daughter cell.
